_meta.rule: An entry requires BOTH a `verification` (what outside the instrument it agrees with) and a `falsification` (the measurement that would have shown it wrong, and its outcome). Inputs -- material properties, physical constants, requirements -- carry `source` instead, and are marked kind=input. Results carry kind=result. error:null means UNMEASURED, never zero.

_meta.indirection: A NAME ALONE MUST NOT RESOLVE. Entries with a `contexts` list hold several recorded values discriminated by context (solver, mesh, extraction, ne, ...). values.get(name, **context) returns one or REFUSES, printing the alternatives. Added 2026-08-25 after CONVENTIONS 7aq/7at: every serious error in that window was one name meaning different measured things in different contexts. Legacy single-value entries (no `contexts`) still resolve.

torch.sapphire.permittivity.material: single-crystal sapphire (Al2O3), eps PERPENDICULAR to the anisotropy (c) axis — what TE011's E_phi sees when c lies along the tube axis
torch.sapphire.permittivity.source: ✅ MEASURED. Krupka J, Huang W-T, Tung M-J, 'Complex permittivity measurements of low-loss microwave ceramics employing higher order quasi TE0np modes excited in a cylindrical dielectric sample', Meas. Sci. Technol. 16 (2005) 1014-1020, doi:10.1088/0957-0233/16/4/014. Figure 10 caption: 'Dielectric loss tangents PERPENDICULAR TO THE ANISOTROPY AXIS ... The measured permittivity was 4.43 +-0.5% for single-crystal quartz and 9.39 +-0.5% for sapphire.' refs/Complex_Permittivity_Measurements_of_Low-Loss_Micr.pdf, supplied by the user 2026-08-25. 🔑 The method is TE0np modes in a cylindrical sample — the SAME mode family as this cavity.
torch.sapphire.permittivity.note: ✅ THE AXIS CORRECTION IS REAL; ITS CONSEQUENCE IS SMALLER THAN FIRST CLAIMED. Measured on this cavity (e3-torch-01 B_sap): eps 11.6 -> 9.39 moves f0 by only +3.325 MHz, a slope of 1.50 MHz per unit eps. The R-era slope of 6.56 used to predict a cancellation is 4.4x too large and does NOT transfer. So the torch shift goes from about -13.9 MHz to about -10.5 MHz -- a 24% reduction, NOT the cancellation predicted. The torch restoration keeps its urgency.
torch.sapphire.permittivity.verification: Independent of this programme, peer-reviewed, quoted uncertainty +-0.5% on the real part. Agrees with the standard uniaxial convention (eps_perp ~9.4 ordinary, eps_par ~11.6 extraordinary) that geometry.py's comment INVERTED.
torch.sapphire.permittivity.falsification: geometry.py:1416 (from R98) asserted '11.6 is eps_PERP_c ... 9.4 is eps_PARALLEL_c'. This measurement says the reverse. R32's supporting check was CIRCULAR: 'c-longitudinal reproduces isotropic 11.6' confirms only that the simulation put 11.6 on the perpendicular axis, which was the assumption under test.

loop.azim.h.mm.description: AZIMUTHAL loop: height of the arc above the barrel wall, i.e. the arc sits at r = a - h. Also sets the conductor-to-wall clearance (h - half the conductor's radial thickness), which is both a capacitance and the arc risk.
loop.azim.h.mm.source: STATED by the user 2026-08-29 as the range to characterise: 2, 3, 4 mm. 🔴 NOT A CHOSEN VALUE — 3.0 is the middle of that range, recorded so the parameter has a home with provenance rather than living as a number on a command line. The sweep is what chooses it.
loop.azim.h.mm.verification: a run that quotes this must be a sweep OVER it, not a run that inherited it

loop.azim.arc.mm.description: AZIMUTHAL loop: ARC LENGTH along the wall. Unwound conductor = arc - port gap + 2h. 🔑 Length not angle: the angle depends on R = a - h, so specifying an angle would couple h and L, and they are meant to be independent axes.
loop.azim.arc.mm.source: STATED by the user 2026-08-29: lambda/10 = 12.24 mm plus brackets at 10.2 and 14.2. lambda/10 puts the loop well BELOW resonance, where it behaves as a lumped inductor — avoiding both the 39.6% conductor loss measured at lambda/4 and the tolerance sensitivity there (d ln Q_ext / d ln L = 4-6.5). 🔴 NOT CHOSEN; 12.24 is the centre of the declared range.

loop.strip.mm.description: Conductor cross-section [axial, radial] for a RECTANGULAR strip, or null for a round wire of loop.wire_r.mm. The AXIAL dimension is the wide one, so the broad face lies parallel to the wall.
loop.strip.mm.source: PROPOSED by the user 2026-08-29: compare a 1 mm round wire against a 5x1 mm strip, broad face to the wall, because the conductor's impedance shows up in the solve. null is the current default (round wire) — the strip is a case the sweep carries, not a choice yet.

provenance.hypothesis: H3 — cavity.Q0.loaded as a function of the PLASMA STATE
provenance.document: NEXT.md § CRITICAL COUPLING FOR N2 DISSOCIATION
provenance.question: Does the azimuthal vacuum pedestal collapse once the arc refinement spans the conductor-to-wall gap? Step 2 of the piece-by-piece bisection.
provenance.why_this_axis: eps and sigma are what MAXWELL sees. Reaching them through plasma.n_e needs BOTH a Saha inversion AND a collision rate, and the collision rate is an UNMADE DECISION: every rig solved NU_M=1e11 while physics.plasma_state gives 6.295e10 from the same temperature — 3.4x in eps, 1.53x in sigma at n_e 7.9e18. h3_loaded.py says 'Decide which before any further loaded number is quoted' and the decision was never made. This axis carries neither assumption and survives the decision either way.
provenance.prior_art: h3-azimne-01 swept 9 DENSITIES (vacuum torch, azimuthal loop) and found the cavity optimum near 3e16. This is the same question re-asked on the axis that does not assume Drude or Saha, on the DESIGN cavity. e0kp_meshfloor: the mesh does not depend on eps or sigma, so all points share ONE cached mesh — same-mesh differencing, mesh noise identically zero across the curve.

parameters.note_cache: ⚠️ The mesh cache is deliberately LEFT ON. eps/sigma never enter the mesher's arguments, so all seven cases hit ONE cached mesh — which is the point: differences across the curve carry zero mesh noise.
parameters.note_coupler: 🔑 PLAIN BARREL LOOP, NO SERIES GAP — and the coupler is a FIXTURE here, not a subject. User, 2026-09-06: *"Does that include a coupler? (I hope not)"* A DRIVEN solve cannot have no port, so the question is how much it contaminates Q0.loaded. MEASURED loss budget at n_e 7.9e18: the plasma is 99.705% of the loaded dissipation and EVERYTHING else — walls + torch + loop — is 0.295%. Swapping the coupler entirely (plain cap vs barrel + gap2 2.25) moves cavity.Q0.loaded by 0.123%; even a 10x lossier coupler moves it 2.6%. So the loaded map is a cavity+plasma property to ~0.1%. ⚠️ THE VACUUM ANCHOR IS NOT: cavity.Q0.cold is 25,416 with gap2 2.25 vs 43,523 for the plain-loop design cavity. That point is an INSTRUMENT CHECK, not a datum. 🔴 gap2 dropped because its basis is retracted (ret:coupling-series-as-design, ret:minimax-q0-105) and the 2026-09-06 decision forbids chasing the barrel — this run must not smuggle that geometry back in as an assumption.
parameters.note_probes: 🔑 |E| INSIDE THE PLASMA — the observable electron-impact dissociation actually needs. Power absorbed by the plasma IS power into the electron cloud (Drude sigma is electron momentum transfer), but whether those electrons DISSOCIATE is set by E/N, i.e. by the field where they are. 🔴 IT CANNOT COME FROM STORED ENERGY: probecheck.py — electric energy goes as eps|E|^2 and eps_eff is NEGATIVE in the metal-like regime, so it goes negative there (measured p_elec = -3e-5). Probes are the only route. ✅ VALIDATED MECHANISM: h3-field-01 (2026-08-26) ran named probes on this cavity and checked them against closed form to 0.6% — E_phi ~ J1(chi'01 r/a) predicts E(8.5)/E(4.25) = 1.974, measured 1.987. THE SAME PAIR IS INCLUDED HERE so every case carries that check. ⚠️ bore_in/mid/edge span the plasma annulus (r = 2.0-8.5 mm). field_peak sits at r = 0.4805a = 42.3 mm, TE011's known maximum, in VACUUM — a landmark that needs no plasma physics to predict (probecheck V3). ⚠️ Probes are read at the SELECTED resonance and are captured even when the 3 dB fit FAILS: |E| does not need a width to exist, and h3-azimload-02 lost a good solve to a failed fit.
parameters.note_geometry: 🔑 standoff 2.0 mm / arc 12.24 mm — h3-azimwidth-01's CHARACTERISED point, where the L-exponents were fitted with the CORRECTED port face (0.9x the conductor's half-extent). ⚠️ NOT h3-azimload-02's standoff 3.0: that run produced no usable loaded number (ret:azimload02-beta-no-resonance) and its geometry has no characterisation behind it.
parameters.note_bisect: 🔑 STEP 2 OF THE AZIMUTHAL BISECTION. ONE VARIABLE: the ARC REFINEMENT REACH. arc_chords is back at 7 and size_factor at 1.0, so this is h3-azimmap-01's vacuum case with ONLY the mesh field around the conductor changed.
parameters.note_readout: 🔴 THE READOUT IS THE OFF-RESONANCE BASELINE |S11| AND error-indicators.csv, NOT A FIT — neither depends on the extraction machinery in doubt. Barrel reference: -0.010 dB, err max 5.85e-3, 346,118 tets.
parameters.note_mechanism: 🔴 THE REFINEMENT BALLS DID NOT REACH THE WALL. geometry.py placed them on the conductor CENTRELINE with radius 2.0*loop_rw = 2.0 mm, but the centreline sits `_hh` = standoff + t/2 from the wall — 3.0 mm at standoff 2, 4.0 mm at standoff 3. So 1.0 / 2.0 mm of the wall gap got cavity-scale elements, in the one place an azimuthal loop's field is strongest. The measured pedestal follows that gap at MATCHED element count: 349,530 tets / 1.0 mm unreached -> -2.456 dB (43% absorbed); 351,049 tets / 2.0 mm unreached -> -3.717 dB (58%). ⚠️ The BARREL loop has no wall gap to span, which is why it was never affected. Fixed 2026-09-06: reach = max(2*rc, _hh + 0.5 mm), i.e. 2.0 -> 3.5 mm here, pinnable as arc_ball_mm.
